text:
alex: Heads-up — since yesterday we've seen multiple tenant tails at 95th token latency spikes when the cluster-autoscaler bounces between adding a whole GPU node and waiting for pods to schedule. Looks like two tenants hit concurrent burst workloads and we get a cold-KV-cache + long pre-launch time.

maria: Yeah saw that too. Which region?

alex: us-west-2 primarily, but also a couple pods in eu-west-1 that flared. autoscaler logs show 3 pods pending -> scale up -> scaled 1 node -> another surge -> scale again. Mean time to ready for a GPU node is ~120s with our current node image + drivers.

jon: We've talked about smaller pools to reduce granularity (eg 1-2 GPU node pools per team) vs large shared pools. Smaller pools = faster targeted scaling but higher idle cost and management complexity.

sam: Also want to call out network egress throttles — some model fetches from s3 in eu-west-3 are slower, so pods there hold GPUs longer. That's region-level constraint causing apparent contention.

alex: Proposal A: carve out tenant-dedicated node pools (1 pool per major customer) with min=0,max=10, taints+tolerations so only tenant namespaces schedule. Pros: isolation, straightforward chargeback via node labels. Cons: many nodepools -> control plane churn, higher baseline.

maria: Proposal B: keep big shared pools but add a "slice" abstraction — use MPS / MIG (NVIDIA) to multiplex multiple pods per GPU, plus a node-level soft-quota controller that enforces per-namespace GPU fractional shares. Pros: better GPU utilization, lower idle cost. Cons: still noisy neighbor risk and some models don't run well under MIG.

jon: Adding cost allocation: we can add node annotation `redwood/cost-center: <team>` and export to billing pipeline. If we create ephemeral slice nodes, we need to tag by slice owner + pool-id.

sam: Quick config sketch for autoscaler we tried locally: ```yaml
# cluster-autoscaler config snippet
--expander=least-waste
--max-nodes-total=200
--balance-similar-node-groups
``` We need `--max-node-provision-time` tuned for our image (increase from default 10m?).

alex: Another axis: pre-warmed standby nodes (keep 1-2 spare in each AZ) so scale-up is just scheduling, not provisioning. Cost is predictable but increases steady-state spend. Would be cheaper than oversubscription penalties.

maria: For dedicated pools, we should also consider kube-scheduler priority + descheduler to move low-priority batch jobs off GPUs quickly during spikes. Right now batch pods sometimes block interactive latency-sensitive pods.

jon: Ops-bot posted autoscaler events: `autoscaler: scaleUp from 0 to 2 (1 nodes added)`, `autoscaler: scaleUp from 2 to 4` — you can see the thrash. Maybe add a scale cooldown or bin-pack policy to avoid split scaling.

ops-bot: Incident note: 1781234567 — autoscaler thrash detected in us-west-2 between 10:12-10:18 UTC; impact=temporary latency increase for tenants: team-alpha, team-gamma.

sam: Cost tradeoff numbers I pulled: keeping 2 pre-warmed p4 nodes per AZ across us-west-2 ~ +$8k/month but reduces latency SLO misses by ~95% for these bursts (based on last 3 weeks).

alex: I'd like a decision framework: (1) strict tenant pools for customers that pay enterprise SLA, (2) shared pools with MIG for default tenants, (3) pre-warmed standby in hot regions, (4) cost labels + export. Also add `taint:dedicated=true:NoSchedule` for strict pools.

maria: Sounds reasonable. One more: for eu-west-3 region we should disable placing large download-heavy models until we migrate model cache to local edge. Right now network IO ties up GPUs.

jon: Action items: 
- jon: prototype MIG-based slice controller + e2e test with worst-case models (ETA 2w)
- alex: run cost/benefit with finance for pre-warmed standby across top-3 regions (ETA 3d)
- sam: add autoscaler flags trial in staging (`--max-node-provision-time=900`, `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m`) and run load test (ETA 4d)
- maria: draft nodepool provisioning playbook for tenant-dedicated pools (include taints, labels, billing tags) (ETA 1w)

alex: If everyone ok, I'll open a PR with the decision matrix and a recommended rollout plan (start with two enterprise customers on dedicated pools, enable MIG for the rest behind a feature flag).

maria: +1. Also add a rollback plan: if MIG causes regressions we flip flag and move back to dedicated scheduling.

sam: +1 from me. Let's keep the eu-west-3 cache work high priority.

jon: +1. We'll keep monitoring autoscaler metrics and add a dashboard widget for node provision time and pending pod counts per tenant.

alex: Cool — I'll create the PR and link the staging experiments. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
